description_good_justification: The README opens with what the package is: an opinionated ESLint configuration for JavaScript, TypeScript and Markdown: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/README.md#eslint-config-phun-ky
interact_justification: The README explains how to install and use the package, and the contributing guide how to give feedback (GitHub issues) and contribute: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_justification: The contribution process (issues, pull requests, checks, sign-off): https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-code
contribution_requirements_justification: Contribution requirements, including coding style and a test for every rule change, are in CONTRIBUTING.md: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#contributing-code
documentation_interface_justification: The interface is the exported configuration. The README shows how to use and override it, the files it covers and the rules it sets: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/README.md#rules
sites_https_justification: The repository and the npm package are served over HTTPS: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests are searchable, addressable by URL and open to anyone with a GitHub account: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/issues
english_justification: All documentation is in English, and reports and comments in English are accepted.
maintained_justification: The project is actively maintained, with releases and changes in November 2026: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/releases
repo_track_justification: Git records who changed what and when: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/commits/main
repo_interim_justification: Every change is a public commit and pull request between releases, not only the releases themselves.
version_unique_justification: Every release has a unique version, tagged as <version>: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/tags
version_semver_justification: Semantic Versioning; a change that makes lint report more problems only comes in a major release: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
version_tags_justification: Each release is tagged in git: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/tags
release_notes_justification: A CHANGELOG.md generated from conventional commits, also published as GitHub release notes: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No release has fixed a publicly known vulnerability in the published package. Such a fix would be listed in the release notes and a GitHub security advisory.
report_responses_justification: Every issue is assigned to the maintainer when it is opened. No one outside the project has filed a bug report in the last 12 months, so none is unanswered.
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are answered in their GitHub issue. No one outside the project has filed one in the last 12 months, so none is unanswered.
report_archive_justification: All issues and pull requests stay public and searchable on GitHub: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports through GitHub private vulnerability reporting or by email: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: Reports are acknowledged within 7 days; no vulnerability has been reported in the last 6 months: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-reports-are-handled
build_justification: There is no build: the package is published as written (index.js): https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#architecture
build_common_tools_justification: There is no build: the package is published as written (index.js): https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#architecture
build_floss_tools_justification: There is no build: the package is published as written (index.js): https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#architecture
test_justification: npm test runs node:test tests that lint snippets with the configuration through ESLint's Node API, and npm run check:pack installs the packed package and lints JavaScript, TypeScript, Markdown and test-file fixtures with it: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
test_invocation_justification: npm test, the standard way to run tests in an npm project: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#development
test_most_justification: npm test covers 100% of the lines, functions and branches of index.js, measured with Node's built-in coverage, and fails below 99% of lines, 100% of functions or 95% of branches. check:pack also lints fixtures with the packed package.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: The Checks workflow lints, checks the format and runs check:pack on Node 24 and Node 22.13.0 for every pull request and every push to main: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/.github/workflows/check.yml
test_policy_justification: A rule change must come with a test, and a bug fix with a test that fails without it: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
tests_are_added_justification: Recent changes came with fixtures: the README example and quotes fixes in 2.0.11 (#99) added check:pack, and linting test files in 3.0.0 (#100) added test fixtures and a TypeScript fixture for the no-undef fix.
tests_documented_added_justification: The tests policy is part of the instructions for contributing code: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
warnings_justification: There is no compiler. ESLint, with this configuration and Prettier, lints every file including Markdown, and Prettier checks the JSON and YAML files.
warnings_fixed_justification: Lint and the format check report no errors and no warnings.
warnings_strict_justification: The repository is linted with every rule the package sets, and lint errors and format problems fail the Checks workflow.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer knows how to design secure software. The principles applied: no code beyond configuration and no dynamic code, few runtime dependencies chosen by a written policy and declared with caret ranges, least-privilege CI tokens, pinned Actions, a ruleset on main, and releases with provenance. What the package guarantees and does not: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the common errors for this kind of software: supply chain (runtime plugins chosen by policy, dependency review and an audit gate before releases, locked development dependencies, pinned Actions), running untrusted code (documented: ESLint and Prettier run JavaScript configuration files from the project being linted), and dynamic code (none): https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
crypto_published_justification: The package implements and calls no cryptography and does no network access: it is ESLint configuration. See the security expectations: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations

delivery_mitm_justification: The package is delivered by npm over HTTPS with Sigstore-signed provenance, and the repository by GitHub over HTTPS.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hashes are fetched over HTTP; npm verifies package integrity from the registry metadata over HTTPS.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: One moderate advisory reaches consumers through typescript-eslint: GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249 in minimatch, public since 2026-10-30. It can't be fixed from this repository until typescript-eslint allows minimatch 11; it is an accepted exception, tracked with its 60-day date (2026-12-29) in https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/issues/114. No other medium or higher vulnerability is known: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerability has been found in the published package or its dependencies.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are in the repository; GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#secrets
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL (GitHub default setup) analyses every pull request and push to main, and ESLint runs on every pull request.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL analyses the JavaScript and the GitHub Actions workflows on every push to main and every pull request, and the ruleset on main requires its results, with no errors and no high or critical security alerts, before merging: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#code-scanning
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CodeQL has no open alerts; the ruleset blocks merging with a high or critical one.
static_analysis_often_justification: On every pull request and every push to main.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No fuzzing or other dynamic analysis tool. check:pack runs the packed package before every release, which is a test rather than dynamic analysis.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: All code is JavaScript on Node.js, which is memory-safe; there is no C, C++ or other memory-unsafe code.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No run-time assertions: the package is configuration data, checked by the fixtures in check:pack.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis is run, so it has found nothing to fix.
achieve_passing_justification: The project has the passing badge: https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/16758
dco_justification: Every commit must be signed off under the Developer Certificate of Origin, checked on every pull request by the DCO app and required by the ruleset on main: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-certificate-of-origin
governance_justification: The maintainer-led governance model and how decisions are made: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md
roles_responsibilities_justification: The maintainer and contributor roles and their responsibilities, and who holds them: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles
access_continuity_justification: One maintainer holds the access to the repository and the npm package today. Releases use npm trusted publishing (no personal token) and the code is MIT-licensed, but no second person holds access yet: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity
bus_factor_justification: The project has one maintainer, so the bus factor is 1: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/graphs/contributors
documentation_roadmap_justification: What the project plans to do and not do until November 2027, linking the issues: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/ROADMAP.md
documentation_architecture_justification: The configuration, how it is checked and the release scripts: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#architecture
documentation_security_justification: What users can and cannot rely on: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations
documentation_quick_start_justification: Requirements, installation and a usage example, which check:pack runs against the packed package: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/README.md#usage
documentation_current_justification: The README usage example is linted with the packed package by check:pack on every pull request and before every release, npm test fails when the README rule table no longer matches the rules index.js sets, and the documents are updated in the same pull request as the change they describe: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
documentation_achievements_justification: The README shows the OpenSSF Best Practices and Scorecard badges: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/README.md
accessibility_best_practices_justificati: The package has no user interface and the project has no website of its own; its documentation is Markdown on GitHub and npm.
internationalization_justification: The package is ESLint configuration and outputs no text for end users; the messages come from ESLint and its plugins.
sites_password_security_justification: The project sites (GitHub and npm) store no passwords for external users.
maintenance_or_update_justification: The current major is supported as a whole, and the previous major gets high and critical security fixes for 6 months after the next one: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerabilities have been reported to the project; the repository has no security advisories.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: Reports are made privately through GitHub private vulnerability reporting or by email. Acknowledgement within 7 days, assessment, a fix in a private GitHub security advisory, coordinated disclosure and credit: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#how-reports-are-handled
coding_standards_justification: Code follows this project's own ESLint configuration and Prettier, and must pass npm run lint and npm run format:check: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#coding-style
coding_standards_enforced_justification: The Checks workflow runs ESLint (with Prettier) and the format check on every pull request, and the ruleset on main requires it to pass before merging.

build_repeatable_justification: There is no build: the package is published as written (index.js): https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#architecture
installation_common_justification: The package is installed and removed with npm: npm install --save-dev eslint-config-phun-ky and npm uninstall eslint-config-phun-ky.
installation_standard_variables_justific: Installation is done entirely by npm, which honours its standard location settings (--prefix, npm_config_prefix, global or local). The package has no install scripts.
installation_development_quick_justifica: git clone, npm ci and npm test give the full development and test environment: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#development
external_dependencies_justification: The dependencies are listed in package.json and locked in package-lock.json: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/package.json
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot checks npm dependencies and GitHub Actions weekly, dependency review checks every pull request, and npm audit runs before every release: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
updateable_reused_components_justificati: No third-party code is copied into the repository; every plugin and config comes from npm through package.json and the lockfile, declared with caret ranges, and Dependabot opens update pull requests.
interfaces_current_justification: The code uses current interfaces: ESLint 10 flat configuration, ES modules, Node 24 in CI, and current GitHub Actions pinned to commit SHAs.
automated_integration_testing_justificat: The Checks workflow lints, checks the format, runs the tests with coverage, and installs the packed package and lints fixtures with it on Node 24 and Node 22.13.0, on every pull request and push to main, reporting results as GitHub checks.
regression_tests_added50_justification: Five of the six bug fixes of the last six months have a test that fails if the bug returns: the TypeScript no-undef fix (#100) and the quotes fix (#99) with tests and fixtures, the README example (#99) with check:pack, Markdown parsing (2.0.10, #87) with a test added in November 2026, and the TypeScript resolver import that crashed on load (2.0.9) with every test, which loads index.js. The sixth removed import-x/no-unused-modules, a rule that does nothing on ESLint 10.
test_statement_coverage80_justification: Statement and line coverage of index.js, measured with Node's built-in coverage on every CI run, is 100%; npm test fails below 99% of lines, 100% of functions or 95% of branches.
test_policy_mandated_justification: A rule change must come with a test, and a bug fix with a test that fails without it: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
implement_secure_design_justification: Secure design principles applied (economy of mechanism, no dynamic code, minimal declared dependencies, least privilege, open design, checks before release): https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#secure-design-principles
crypto_algorithm_agility_justification: The package implements and calls no cryptography and does no network access: it is ESLint configuration. See the security expectations: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#security-expectations

signed_releases_justification: Releases are published from GitHub Actions with npm trusted publishing and carry Sigstore-signed provenance; the signing identity comes from GitHub OIDC, not a key on npm. version_tags_signed_justification: Release tags are annotated but not signed; releases are verified through npm provenance instead.
input_validation_justification: The package takes no input: it exports configuration, and ESLint validates every rule's options against the rule's schema when it loads the configuration.
hardening_justification: No eval or dynamic code, no state, runtime dependencies chosen by policy, read-only CI permissions with SHA-pinned actions, CodeQL on every change, an audit gate and a pack check before every release.
assurance_case_justification: What is protected, the threat model, trust boundaries, secure design principles, the common weaknesses countered and the known gaps: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md
osps_ac_01_01_justification: The maintainer, the only person with access, uses two-factor authentication on GitHub, which GitHub requires for code contributors. Anyone given access later must use it too: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#becoming-a-maintainer
osps_ac_02_01_justification: GitHub requires a role to be chosen for every collaborator invited to the repository, and the governance requires the lowest role that fits: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#becoming-a-maintainer
osps_ac_03_01_justification: The ruleset on main requires changes to arrive through a pull request with passing checks. Only the maintainer, as administrator, can bypass it, which the release workflow uses to push its commit and tag.
osps_ac_03_02_justification: A separate ruleset on main, with no bypass, blocks deleting the branch and force pushes.
osps_br_01_01_justification: No workflow interpolates untrusted metadata, such as pull request titles or branch names, into a script; github.actor is passed through an environment variable: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml

osps_vm_03_01_justification: Private reporting through GitHub private vulnerability reporting or the security email: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories when fixed: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/security/advisories
osps_ac_04_02_justification: Each job declares only the permissions it needs, for example the labeler has pull-requests: write and publishing has id-token: write: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/.github/workflows/label.yml
osps_br_01_04_justification: Workflows take no manual inputs, and the only collaborator-controlled value used, github.actor, is passed through an environment variable: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml
osps_br_02_02_justification: Each release is a versioned npm package and a GitHub release with the same tag, and its SBOM is named eslint-config-phun-ky-<version>.cdx.json: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/releases
osps_br_07_02_justification: How secrets are stored, accessed and rotated: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#secrets
osps_do_03_01_justification: How to verify release integrity with npm audit signatures: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_do_03_02_justification: How to check that a release was built by the publish workflow in phun-ky/eslint-config, from its provenance: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_do_04_01_justification: The current major (3.x) is supported as a whole; the previous major gets high and critical security fixes for 6 months after the next major is released: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
osps_do_05_01_justification: A major stops getting security updates 6 months after the next major is released: 2.x on 10 May 2027; 1.x and older, and 2.0.0 to 2.0.9, are no longer supported: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#supported-versions
osps_gv_04_01_justification: Collaborators are reviewed, including two-factor authentication, before getting escalated permissions: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#becoming-a-maintainer
osps_qa_02_02_justification: The publish workflow attaches a CycloneDX SBOM of the runtime dependencies to each GitHub release from the first release after 3.0.0; the releases up to 3.0.0 have none: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#verifying-releases
osps_qa_04_02_justification: The project has a single repository, so there are no subprojects in other repositories.
osps_qa_06_02_justification: When and how the tests run, locally and in CI: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
osps_qa_06_03_justification: Rule changes and bug fixes must come with tests: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#tests
osps_qa_07_01_justification: The project has one maintainer, so no non-author approval is possible yet. A review by a maintainer other than the author is required once there is a second maintainer: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#reviews
osps_sa_03_02_justification: Threat model, trust boundaries and attack surface: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/ASSURANCE.md#threat-model
osps_vm_04_02_justification: Vulnerabilities in dependencies that don't affect the project are recorded as OpenVEX statements: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/vex.openvex.json
osps_vm_05_01_justification: Thresholds for fixing vulnerability and licence findings in dependencies: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
osps_vm_05_02_justification: Releases are blocked while a runtime dependency has a known high or critical vulnerability (npm audit in the publish workflow): https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#dependencies
osps_vm_05_03_justification: Dependency review checks every pull request against the GitHub Advisory Database and blocks high or critical findings, as the documented policy says: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/.github/workflows/dependency-review.yml
osps_vm_06_02_justification: The ruleset on main blocks merging while CodeQL reports an error or a high or critical security alert: https://github.com/phun-ky/eslint-config/blob/main/SECURITY.md#code-scanning
